finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters run arbitrary commands on the server.

trace.note: String concatenation 'ping -c 1 ' + req.query.host passed to exec(), which spawns /bin/sh -c
Command stdout returned in the response, so output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping. No auth middleware. No use of execFile or argument arrays. The server listens on port 3001 without host binding. Also, req.query.host can be an array or object (Express qs parsing), but that does not stop injection. Example: /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id or $(cat /etc/passwd).

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to exec() (shell) with no validation, no auth middleware (the only app.* calls are routes and app.listen at line 28), and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so an anonymous request such as /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id runs arbitrary commands. Output is returned only when the shell exits 0, which holds when the injected command is last.
